head: 969886ba03761bae2f2fae543eb6815960b9fc98
blocking: B1 (standards; fail-closed, README contract vs reference): contracts/README.md:160/:168/:191-192 say a placed phrase occupies every bar its span touches and that tempo_conflict means 'a change inside its bars' (and :153 'refuse, never ... retime'), but songform.py:51-54 only checks (anchor, end). A source tempo change after a phrase's last note inside its last bar is assembled, not refused, and silently dropped: ph1 [0,5760) in 4/4 with a change at 6720 (or 5760) assembles with tempo map [(0, 500000)], so the bars play 4.0 s instead of the source's 4.1 s (4.2 s); a change in the leading rest of a pickup's first bar does refuse (asymmetric). No vector covers it: the README-consistent patch (check (anchor, anchor + bars*bar)) passes all 23 vectors and validate.py -v, so a twin or the T28 runtime written from the README would diverge from the reference undetected, and the PR's claim 'every unsupported mapping refuses ... nothing ... retimed' is not yet true. Fix: check tempo (and meter, for symmetry) over the phrase's whole bars and add a refusal vector (tempo change after a phrase's last note, inside its last bar). Evidence: T02c-review-07-tempo-inside-bars.log, T02c-review-09b-*.
non_blocking: Unpinned layout rule (spec pass 'medium', verified): no committed source marks a phrase ending mid-bar, so the whole-bar round-up (songform.py:62) and 'two phrases never share a bar' (README:164) are unpinned; a floor-instead-of-ceil mutant passes the full gate (T02c-review-09a, validate log byte-identical to head's). The documented consequence (ph1 [0,5760), ph2 [5760,7680): ph2 moves 5760 -> 9600 in a 3-bar section or in T28's default one-section-per-phrase form; the source's own 2 bars refuse phrase_overflow) is deterministic and in README 'Still open', so not silent. Add that case as an assembled vector and note it for T28.

Unpinned capture inheritance: a mutant comparing only transcription (rules.py:927) passes the gate (T02c-review-11-*-L3); add a scenario with a wrong 1.1 capture_sha256. Also unpinned: the all-instrumental fallback (songform.py:114-115), the raise paths (songform.py:68-71), and half-up rounding in the songform family (all four end_frame values are exact; tempo.json still covers rounding).

Consumers manifest accuracy: fixture.songform omits ace-routes although T48's acceptance reads 'assemble-audio produces slices whose boundaries equal the SongForm vector's frames' (ace-routes is only on the form field); fixture.meter lists guide (T29 has no bar or beat criterion) and omits abc-emission (T56 'full bars'), timeline (T77 'zooms in bars and beats') and midi-in-out (T25). The issue's named consumers (song-spec, guide, abc-emission) are present and every slug is real.

Meter vectors (lead's addendum) are delivered (27 hand-derived cases, re-derived by the reviewer) but cover one valid map with denominators 4 and 8 only; add a second map and denominators 1, 2, 16, 32. timemodel.position/tick_at raise bare ValueError for tick < 0 or bar/beat < 1 (timemodel.py:74, :84; songform._plan :70 likewise) while README:205 names only MeterError codes for the twin; these inputs are outside fixture-meter's schema domain, so document them as input errors.

Documentation drift: README:133 still says the manifest 'is deliberately scoped to vector kinds' and consumers.json keeps scope 'vector-kinds' while adding fields; architecture section 4.6 assemble(melody, form) -> melody vs the reference assemble(melody, song, output) (T28 to reconcile); the preparation doc's first hand-derived case is not a committed vector (the reference reproduces it: 3840/4800/7680/8640, end 11520).

Annotation-driven manifest: fields tracks only locations carrying $comment 'added in 1.x.y' (an unannotated minor addition escapes), each 1.1 gate is a hand-written allOf (shotgun surgery), and ADDED (vector_discovery.py:7) also matches 'added in 1.0.0'. Adequate for the slice; the full consumer inventory stays T02.

Rule tightenings apply to 1.0.0 records too (melody.wellformed bar-line meter rule, rules.py:1050-1052; exact inheritance of a non-null 1.0 lineage). Disclosed, vacuous for every pre-existing record (0 of 19 base tempo maps has more than one meter segment, T02c-review-13; every pre-existing scenario still fires exactly its rules) and consistent with ADR-0033 (bar/beat positions are well defined across meter segments only from bar lines; tick-frame rounding untouched).

Smells (judgement): duplicated tempo-map check (songform.py:68-70 vs melody.wellformed and timemodel._segments) and bar-line derivation (rules.py:1051 vs bar_segments); test_songform.py setUp/run_cli copied from test_vector_discovery.py; HYMN_* restates the world hymn (reviewer verified they are equal today); tuple-typed time, bar segments and _layout return; GLOSSARY nits: 'bar grid' (README:155, songform docstring) uses the Tempo map avoid word 'grid', _layout uses the SongForm avoid word 'layout', _plan vs Score.plan, lineage holds a melody id (rules.py:1066); no GLOSSARY entry for 'pickup' or 'chord symbol' (disclosed).

Pre-existing, outside the diff (follow-up): lane.record_eligible checks a transcription's eligible_lanes against its transcriber but never its license_chain; a Basic Pitch transcription carrying pYIN's chain on both the source and its 1.1.0 assembled copy yields 0 findings (T02c-review-17). Lanes cannot widen (computed from the profile), but obligations could be laundered at the source.

Size: 724 added lines of hand-written Python (627 non-blank: reference 259, vector data 350, generator hooks 53, tests 62) plus 205 schema, 30 manifest and 84 README lines, against the ~400 aim (PR states ~711). It did not impair review; the meter family, added at the lead's request, would have fit a separate PR.

Merge order with #128 (T02d, 19985b8) and #130 (T02b, dd300ff), both on 7cb7bbd. This PR keeps consumers.json at version 1 / scope 'vector-kinds' and adds a fields map checked both ways by added_fields() (discovery accepts keys within {version, scope, consumers, fields}); #130 moves it to version 2 / scope 'vector-kinds and record fields' with keys exactly {version, scope, consumers, records, pending} (MANIFEST_KEYS, set equality) plus known_tickets() and check_records(); #128 only adds consumers['fixture.midi']. Each discovery refuses the other's manifest. Whichever of #130/#131 lands second must, in one commit: (1) set consumers.json to version 2 with keys {version, scope, consumers, records, pending, fields} and one agreed scope string; consumers = the union (tempo, status, recommend, ledger, audition, binding, songform, meter, and midi once #128 lands) with each list unchanged; records and pending exactly as #130 (melody-spec and song-spec stay pending, so their 1.1.0 additions stay covered by fields); fields exactly as #131; (2) in vector_discovery.py add 'fields' to MANIFEST_KEYS as a required key, keep #130's version/scope check, known_tickets, check_tickets and check_records, keep #131's added_fields() set comparison and its 'missing ... orphan ...' message, and validate every fields list through check_tickets(known_tickets); when a pending kind later moves into records, map its top-level added fields there too; (3) keep both PRs' tests (#130's record-consumer tests; #131's test_songform.py, whose subtests edit fields and match 'missing', 'orphan' and 'unknown consumer ticket slug', the last also matching #130's 'duplicate or unknown consumer ticket slug'); (4) keep both generate_fixtures.py hooks, regenerate, and re-prove byte identity of every fixture then on integration plus validate.py -v. Whichever of #128/#131 lands second: keep the 'MIDI round trip (T02d)' and 'SongForm assembly (T02c)' README sections (and #130's 'Evidence-binding inputs (T02b)'), merge the shared 'Not covered yet' line (T02c rewrites 'SongForm assembly ...', T02d drops 'the MIDI round trip'), and, because #131 makes an off-bar meter change break melody.wellformed while #128's from_smf accepts a time signature at any tick (it checks only 1 <= nn <= 32 and dd <= 5), add a typed MidiRefusal for a time signature off a bar line with a refusal vector (or record it open in #128's README); #128's only meter change (3/4 at 3840) already lands on a bar line.

Base drift: integration advanced from 7cb7bbd to dee28e2 during the review (#129, T03 license verification, merged 2026-11-08T02:29Z; no file overlap with #131), so #131 is BEHIND. A local trial merge of dee28e2 into 969886b (never pushed, noreply identity) keeps the reviewed patch-id 7f9d4bf57616be55f303aa980ee58d70682f90b4 and passes the full local gate and validate.py -v (T02c-review-18-*). This review carries to an updated head only while that patch-id is unchanged; B1's fix changes the patch and needs a fresh review.
